newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve bigger Community share in EBRD.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve bigger Community share in EBRD.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Friday plans to increase the European Community's contribution to share capital in the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
Draft decision COM(96)377 provides for the Community to increase its participation following the decision by the bank's board last April to double the EBRD's capital to 20 billion Ecus.
The Community holds a 300-million-Ecu share of the original 10-million-Ecu capital.
The EBRD was set up after the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1989 to help fund the transformation of the former Soviet bloc countries to a market economy.
By December 1995, the bank had approved 368 operations in 24 countries at a total cost of eight billion Ecus.
The board predicted the bank would reach the 10-billion-Ecu ceiling for outstanding loans by spring 1997, and had the choice of increasing its capital or limiting future operations.
